text: Use case: illustration-story. One full 16:9 finished cel-anime frame for the opening of a basketball scene. Reference input is the approved full-scene style and all character identity. Draw a tight cinematic medium close-up of Kaede Rukawa in red SHOHOKU 11, black straight fringe, pale warm skin, slim teenage proportions, black left wristband. His eyes are intensely fixed on the off-screen basket to the left; the face is handsome and calm, clearly the SAME Rukawa as reference. Show natural hands supporting ONE orange basketball near his upper chest, shooting hand under/back and guide hand on side; arms connected naturally, no contorted fingers. Crop just below jersey number near waist, full head and fingertips stay within frame. Keep 1990s hand-drawn anime ink, restrained warm cel colors, consistent two-tone shading, muted teal gym background with small unified gallery crowd and windows softly simplified at depth. Background figures use the same visual language as the hero, no photographic bokeh or realistic skin. Shallow staging but no blurry face. Single overhead gym light direction. No captions, scoreboard, framing border, labels, panel grid or UI. This will be animated by a local video model, so leave modest margin around head/hands and keep the detailed identity clean.

Use case: illustration-story. ONE finished 16:9 hand-drawn basketball anime background frame, a basket close-up in the EXACT same gym and 1990s cel style as the reference. Camera looks up slightly at the hoop, backboard occupying upper middle/right and gym teal wall/windows/roof beams behind. Orange basketball rim is near center at x56%, y40%, seen from a low three-quarter angle as a clearly readable ellipse, correct rigid geometry, white painted rectangle on the transparent glass board, metal support on right. A natural hanging white knotted basketball net is attached around the rim and hangs down to y70%, clean and legible without overcomplicated duplicate lines. Make the basket, rim, net and characters use a consistent hand-inked drawing, modest flat color and warm/cool cel shading. Packed spectators with raised hands and red towels appear in the lower gallery/background under the basket; correct small scale and simplified anime faces like the reference. Warm gym light and muted teal palette. ONE orange basketball is approaching from the upper left, above the rim, about a ball diameter away from the mouth; ball size physically fits within rim (diameter roughly half opening width). It is clearly outside/above the net and not touching backboard or rim. This frame precedes a clean swish; plenty of space for the ball to fall through the hoop. No players blocking the rim. No text overlays, scoreboard, captions, panels, photoreal texture or 3D render. One coherent drawn scene, not separate pasted objects.

Use case: illustration-story. ONE finished widescreen 16:9 frame from the SAME coherent 1990s basketball anime as the reference input. The decisive three-pointer has just scored. Medium-wide on the COURT: Kaede Rukawa in red SHOHOKU 11, slim black straight fringe, black left wristband, calmly looking left toward the basket, shoulders relaxed after landing, both feet grounded; his red-haired teammate Sakuragi in SHOHOKU 10 is a few steps to his left turning toward him excitedly with a clenched fist, and muscular tall Akagi in red SHOHOKU 4 farther left smiling as he releases his box-out stance. The white-and-blue RYONAN 7 defender is farther behind, disappointed, lowering his arms. All are recognizable as the exact same characters, hair, body proportions and uniforms in the reference. Place the people at the proper scales and depths on ONE shared court plane; natural knees, elbows, hands, shared overhead lighting, grounded contact shadows. Show clear room between the teammates for them to approach and celebrate. Above the muted teal wall, a packed gallery crowd has just begun lifting arms and red towels in celebration. Same hand-painted wood and windows, all consistent two-tone cel shading, line weight and visual detail. Balanced cinematic layout, all heads and shoes within safe margin. No frozen cutout look, no model turntable, no huge poster-like face, no 3D rendering or photoreal texture. No captions, scoreboard, text outside uniforms, UI or panels.

Use case: illustration-story. One widescreen 16:9 finished 1990s hand-drawn sports anime frame for the quiet final shot AFTER a basketball victory. Reference input fixes the exact visual style and Kaede Rukawa identity. Draw a cinematic chest-up close-up of the SAME slim teenage Rukawa in red SHOHOKU 11, black straight fringe, sharply defined handsome eyes and small calm mouth, slight sweat at temple, natural neck and shoulders, one relaxed exhale. He looks slightly left and downward with restrained satisfaction, head in right half of frame, face at three-quarter view; keep full hair/head in frame with space above. No ball in hands or in frame after victory. Background is the same muted teal gym and gallery with small cheering anime spectators and red towels, drawn simply at depth. Consistent clean ink, natural anatomy, two-tone cel shade, warm skin and gym overhead light. Rukawa should look like the reference, NOT muscular mature man, photoreal human or 3D puppet. Composition leaves calmer darker teal space on left for an eventual minimal score overlay. No actual captions, text overlays, framing devices or panels. One integrated scene, not a pasted portrait.
Additional reference 2 is the approved Rukawa close-up: prioritize its exact facial identity and matching line work; change from tense pre-shot concentration to restrained post-victory calm. Reference 1 fixes the gym and overall palette.
